name: Burrow Pages
description: Your static websites on your own addresses: from GitHub or GitLab (any number of accounts, built in a container when they need it), from any Git repository, from an upload, a repository's own Pages site, or a site that lives elsewhere. Every push deployed, any deploy one click from live again, visitor numbers without cookies, health checks, and your login, a password or public for each.
author: Alexd Aero

actions.label: Pause every site
actions.confirm: Every site stops answering until you resume it. Nothing is deleted.

settings.label: GitHub app client ID
settings.help: The GitHub OAuth app “Sign in with a code” uses (device flow). Burrow Pages' own is filled in; its client ID is public and there is no secret. Burrow Pages → Settings can override it too.

update_card.title: {name} {version}
update_card.tagline: As many GitHub and GitLab accounts as you like, any Git repository by address, and a repository's own Pages site on your address.
highlights: Any number of GitHub and GitLab accounts, each with its own sign-in
An expired sign-in says so on that account (Sign in again), never as a sign-out
Any public Git repository by its https address: Codeberg, Bitbucket, Gitea…
A repository's own GitHub or GitLab Pages site, served on your address with a cache
Rebuilt in 2.0: its own app, builds, uploads, rollbacks, analytics, public sites
